The water-filled candidate is the Euclidean projection of the preliminary sphere center, and Hall prefix inequalities independently place it inside the Minkowski-sum polytope. A convex combination of tangent-face vertices yields a global lower bound for every proposed sphere center with an exact nonnegative center-shift term. The contact count includes equality ties. All finite vertices in dimensions 2 through 12 were exhaustively checked by the included exact-arithmetic code; the analytic steps prove all dimensions.

value.rationale: This gives exact unique Euclidean circumspheres and every contact for a canonical and literature-defined family of combinatorial cubes. The contact face has dimension asymptotic to (3/2)^(1/3)n^(2/3), even though the ambient cube dimension is n-1 and the number of vertices is exponential. This is a sharp geometric screening law rather than routine small cases or an arbitrary numerical invariant.
